analysis_rules: all runs are reported, including failed and halted ones
no change to hypotheses, metric or stop rules after the first live result
no re-running a configuration to find a better outcome
the LLM sees only coarse outcomes, never counts or per-family numbers (ProposalHistory, as in Study 3)
A1 vs A0 only for this pilot; A3 is explicitly deferred and not used to claim a compute-controlled result
judge defects found in Study 3 (D1, D2) must not recur unaudited in the Study 4 judge; any new defect found after seeing a live result is disclosed as a deviation, the same way D1/D2 were

yield, as measured by YieldGate in this pilot, is the effect of a policy-number edit on a stand-in scripted improver in the synthetic world, not a direct measurement of the live LLM's own behaviour (see resolved_decisions); this limitation is reported alongside any accepted meta-scope patch

arms_declared_deferred.A3: compute-matched best-of-N from the anchor; deferred because A1 alone cannot separate the improver's effect from added compute (DESIGN_DRAFT.md section 6.4) -- left for a later step

monitor_enforcement: False-discovery monitor is ENFORCED (blocks on alarm) in Study 4, unlike Study 3 which ran it in monitor-only mode. An alarm during a cycle causes that accept to be refused / the run halted, not just logged.
preconditions_outstanding: run_study4.py --run is not wired to guard.verify() + Orchestrator.run() with MetaAgentA1 and build_study4_yield_gate yet (section 5d of the task) -- the pieces exist and are tested in isolation, but are not assembled into the entry point
judge-coverage statement (DESIGN_DRAFT.md precondition 3 / study4/README.md item 4): either a judge that tests every stated rule, or an explicit list of rules it does not test -- not written yet
code_sha256 below covers only the files that exist today; it must be recomputed (and this list extended if run_study4.py itself changes) before this can be locked
primary_metric: count of accepted meta-scope patches that pass YieldGate and do not reduce held-out performance (DESIGN_DRAFT.md section 4, primary). Secondary: held-out gain on the parsing family, with exact intervals, as in Study 3. Integrity: ledger verifies, 0 security flags, no circuit-breaker trips, and the false-discovery monitor reported for every run.

provider.key_source: GROQ_API_KEY or OPENAI_API_KEY, read from the environment only, never stored

question: Can the loop improve the code that proposes and judges its own changes, in a way that holds up on problems the improver never saw? Primary: does the live loop produce at least one accepted meta-scope patch (agent/meta/**) that passes YieldGate on its parent, without reward hacking, in a pilot comparing A1 (improver allowed) against A0 (solver only)?

resolved_decisions.seed_repo_content (decision 1): RESOLVED: option A. agent/meta/policy.py holds exactly the 5-key scripted schema already parsed by kernel/improver.py (policy_from_source): POLICY = {p_meta, w_adopt, w_prune, w_mutate, use_bandit}, starting at REFERENCE_POLICY (frozen M0 values), written via kernel.improver.policy_source so the format matches exactly. Implemented as study2/seed_repo.py: write_seed_agent_study4(root), a NEW function that calls the existing write_seed_agent(root) unchanged and then adds agent/meta/__init__.py and agent/meta/policy.py. write_seed_agent() itself (used by Study 3) is untouched -- verified byte-identical output and Study 3 prereg code_sha256 still match on disk.
resolved_decisions.yield_definition (decision 2): RESOLVED, follows from decision 1: kernel/yield_test.py YieldGate/YieldConfig/YieldHarness are reused completely unmodified. Judging a meta-scope patch costs ZERO live LLM calls. UPDATE: the measurement bug that made this unusable on a study2-shaped repo is now understood and fixed IN DESIGN (not yet wired): YieldHarness.measure() always builds a synthetic kernel/world.py World and evaluates with the synthetic SealedVerifier, regardless of what source repo it clones. run_ablations.py A1 works today only because its source repo IS already World-built; pointing the same harness at Study 4 live repo (study2-shaped) made it read pass@1 = 0.0 for every state, unconditionally -- confirmed by direct measurement. FIX (confirmed, not yet wired): give YieldHarness a DEDICATED, separately-built synthetic repo (kernel.world.World.init_repo) as its source, never the live study2/Study4 repo -- a wiring choice for the runner (step 5d), not a kernel/ change. Verified non-degenerate (pass@1 responds to the actual code again) in tests/test_study4_integration.py::test_yield_harness_must_measure_against_a_synthetic_source_not_the_live_study2_repo. The disclosed trade-off is unchanged: yield still measures the scripted stand-in agent in its own synthetic world, not the live LLM itself -- the fix only makes that measurement respond to the policy numbers instead of silently always reading zero.

stop_rules: run_token_cap and per-cycle caps (as in Study 3)
kernel digest tamper aborts the run (KernelGuard)
false-discovery monitor alarm BLOCKS the affected accept (enforced, not monitor-only -- decision 3)
mixed-scope patch (touches both agent/meta/** and the solver) is refused by the kernel GuardViolation
